newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures widen losses as rally stalled.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures widen losses as rally stalled.

text.p: Nearby LIFFE robusta coffee futures widened losses in the London afternoon to end Friday sharply down as scale-up origin offers stalled this week's fund-led rally.

July's attempt to clear the psychological $1,800 a tonne mark tumbled as Indonesian and Vietnamese sellers unloaded their holdings. Some Indonesian sellers were away for a local holiday on Thursday when prices took a sharp upward move.
The benchmark contract propelled to a new eight-week-peak at $1,793 a tonne, just $7 short of the $1,800 target, on light fund and arbitrage buying.
But producer selling, end-of-the-week book-squaring and long liquidation pulled prices back to close $22 down at $1,758.
Like in New York, activity was fairly subdued. By the close, 4,530 lots changed hands.

But distant November and January bucked the trend to finish higher. Traders said recent hike in retail arabica prices and possible improved usage of robustas in coffee blends aided good roaster demand.
Technically, July faces a stiff resistance at its life-of-contract high of $1,820. But support is seen intact at $1,700.
Traders said the market's prospects hinged on renewed fund buying.
"Without any fund support, the market will probably hang around here or turn softer," said one.

The rally earlier this week encouraged Vietnamese producers to unload their stocks, traders in Vietnam said. But there are only 20,000 tonnes of coffee left from the current crop after some 270,000 tonnes sold so far.
Vietnamese prices were quoted at $1,460 a tonne FOB Saigon on Thursday, up sharply from $1,360 earlier in the week.
In other news, Brazil portworkers, as expected, returned to work at Santos on Friday. Traders had said the 24-hour stoppage would be short-lived and would have no disruption to coffee shipments.
Options volume totalled 569 lots. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171542 4985
